bull.b: Very low leverage provides durable financial flexibility: it reduces refinancing and covenant risk, preserves ability to fund debottlenecking and early capex internally, and gives time to secure project partners for NorthStar without immediate distress financing, supporting multi‑quarter execution.

A substantial swing to positive adjusted EBITDA and higher revenue reflect improving operating leverage and commercialization scale. Sustained EBITDA generation increases self‑funding capacity, reduces dependence on external capital, and is a durable precursor to eventual positive operating cash flow if maintained.

bull.t: Commercial traction in carbon/CDR and partnerships
bull.b: Recurring sales of carbon attributes and CDR credits to corporate buyers point to a durable revenue stream adjacent to fuels. Corporate demand and Verity partnerships create diversified commercial channels and price discovery that can sustainably enhance margins beyond fuel sales over multiple quarters.

bear.t: Negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Persistent cash burn forces reliance on funding or balance sheet resources until operations are cash‑positive. Even with EBITDA gains, negative OCF/FCF implies timing gaps (tax credit monetization) and raises risk of dilution or higher‑cost project financing, constraining multi‑quarter investment flexibility.

bear.t: Partial offtake coverage & project financing risk
bear.b: Material offtake shortfall is a durable gating item for NorthStar financing and FID. Without additional contracted volumes or stronger lender terms, the company faces higher financing costs and execution delays, which can push back project EBITDA contribution and prolong reliance on corporate funding sources.

bear.t: Ongoing GAAP losses and negative net margin
bear.b: Negative GAAP profitability indicates costs below gross profit still pressure the bottom line. Until the company converts positive gross margins and EBITDA into sustained net income, it will struggle to build retained earnings and internal capital for growth, keeping long‑term financial resilience uncertain.
